overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the ADA accommodation-request language on the meeting notices was a request, not a precondition. It also reminded the bodies of complaint-review duties, which were not raised in the complaints.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the bodies' meeting notices required people needing ADA accommodations to request them two weeks ahead, which violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the language found on each meeting notice complies with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaints: the City Solicitor responded to the complaints before the public bodies met to review them. The AG reminded the bodies of the review requirement.
allegations.key_passage: The chair is required to disseminate copies and the public body must meet to review the complaint and formulate a response, or meet to delegate that authority.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
